definition: Terry Allen Winograd (born February 24, 1946) is an American computer scientist.
details: Pioneered natural language understanding in block-world environments and introduced the Winograd Schema Challenge for AI reasoning. He is a professor at Stanford University, and co-director of the Stanford Human–Computer Interaction Group. He is known within the philosophy of mind and artificial intelligence fields for his work on natural language using the SHRDLU program.

explainer.lead: Terry Winograd is an American professor. His work spans computer science, informatics, artificial intelligence and philosophy of mind.
explainer.knownFor: In addition to the Computer Science Dept., Winograd is associated with the Hasso Plattner Institute of Design at Stanford, also known as the "d.school", which he helped found.

contributions.name: He wrote SHRDLU as a PhD thesis at MIT in the years from 1968–70.
Winograd built a blocks world, restricting the program's intellectual world to a simulated "world of toy blocks".
In 1973, Winograd moved to Stanford University and developed an AI-based framework for understanding natural language which was to give rise to a series of books.
They published a critical appraisal from a perspective based in phenomenology as Understanding Computers and Cognition: a new foundation for design in 1986.
In general, Winograd's work at Stanford has focused on software design in a broader sense than software engineering.

timeline.what: Winograd grew up in Colorado and graduated from Colorado College in 1966.
Receives the IJCAI Computers and Thought Award
Starting in 1995, Winograd served as adviser to Stanford PhD student Larry Page, who was working on a research project involving web search.
In 2002, Winograd took a sabbatical from teaching and spent some time at Google as a visiting researcher.
